A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoLingo and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Existing content can be matched reliably across citation changes, table renumbering, and appendix reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation benchmarks, ablations, user-study outcomes, and robot-controller demonstrations in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds an inference-time and generation-quality study in appendix Table 7.

M1.justification: The semantic autoencoder, repetitive-token filtering, text cross-attention, and masked rectified-flow generation procedure remain unchanged. Equation (7) explicitly specializes the already described linear interpolation. The revised 272D latent configuration uses options already explored in v1.

E1.justification: Both use HumanML3D, its 272D variant, BABEL annotations, and the existing humanoid-controller scenario. The additional inference-step experiments vary computation within retained coverage rather than introducing new data or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1, the MotionStreamer and TMR-263 comparisons, qualitative comparisons, and user studies. MoMask, DisCoRD, and MotionStreamer remain the user-study baselines. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported CFG scale from 6.0 to 5.5. The 272D comparison changes from 4× downsampling with 16-dimensional latents to 2× with 32-dimensional latents. New Table 7 varies inference and sampling steps; the default remains 16 and 32 respectively. These are localized setting revisions and an added evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New appendix Table 7 studies sensitivity to auto-regressive inference steps and flow-sampling steps, measuring the runtime–quality tradeoff. Existing analyses of conditioning, semantic regularization, latent size, adapter depth, and repetitive-token filtering retain their experimental questions.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over 20 runs with 95% confidence intervals for benchmark comparisons. No changed run-count, seed policy, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test is documented. Updated interval values are numerical-result changes.

E6.justification: Reported diversity and reconstruction outcomes change substantially. Table 1 revises VAE/SAE MModality from 2.307/2.215 to 1.414/1.226, altering diversity rankings; SAE FID/Top-1 changes from 0.064/0.542 to 0.066/0.544. Under the revised 272D configuration, rFID/MPJPE changes from 0.280/23.01 mm to 0.026/9.87 mm, while Top-1 changes from 0.788 to 0.776. TMR-263 FID changes from 0.014 to 0.015 and MModality from 21.235 to 20.400. New Table 7 adds runtime–quality results spanning 0.83–9.02 seconds. Changed settings prevent treating all updates as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equation (7) replaces the derivative-based velocity target with epsilon minus the clean latent and explicitly states alpha=1−t and sigma=t. This is algebraically equivalent to the linear interpolation already described in v1, rather than new mathematical reasoning. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantically aligned motion latents, multi-token cross-attention, masked rectified-flow generation, and state-of-the-art benchmark and user-study performance. The appendix additions do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a speed–quality interpretation supporting subsecond generation and the default step counts. Its claim that more steps consistently improve FID and R-Precision overstates Table 7, whose values are not uniformly monotonic. The MotionStreamer table caption also changes from comparable MPJPE to improved MPJPE attributed to replicated padding. The hand-motion limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly supplies the linear flow schedules, revises the documented CFG and 272D latent settings, and expands inference-cost information beyond one runtime. Architecture specifications, training budgets, hardware, and the promise to release code and models otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds 12 works, including NRDF, FrankenMotion, CLoSD, and UniPhys, without removing existing references. These extend citations within existing motion-generation categories and the robot-transfer discussion; the substantive novelty positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include localized grammar corrections, a rewritten inference-speed paragraph, an added affiliation and funding acknowledgment, and revised references to demonstration material. The main section order and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a compact inference-time table, renumbers subsequent appendix tables, and reflows supplementary text. Some captions and result highlighting change. Existing architecture diagrams, qualitative panels, plots, and the user-study interface are retained.

improvement.justification: The new speed–quality sweep provides useful evidence for choosing inference settings where v1 reported only one runtime; explicit flow schedules also improve clarity. These limited benefits are tempered by overstated monotonic-improvement wording and Section 4.3 retaining Top-1 0.542 despite Table 1 reporting 0.544. Revised scores under changed configurations do not themselves establish better paper quality.
